newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: New Zealand dollar ends steady, market becalmed.
newsitem.headline: New Zealand dollar ends steady, market becalmed.

text.p: The New Zealand dollar's rollercoaster ride over the last few days came to an end on Thursday but dealers said the relative calm was likely to be shortlived.
The Kiwi was at US$0.6972/79 in late trade and at 66.57 on the Trade-Weighted Index, barely changed from its opening levels, having traded a 0.6965-80 range.
Dealers said retail sales data, which showed a 0.6 percent seasonally adjusted decline in August, was responsible for taking the currency to its early session lows.
But the weakness met with renewed demand, particularly from Tokyo, in the afternoon, taking the Kiwi up to session highs.

"The market is still pretty nervy and reactionary to comments, particularly when you see the Reserve Bank and politicians reacting," said one dealer. "We have not seen those comments today, so hence the quite narrow ranges," he said.
The week started with post-election bullishness which was later followed by bearishness inspired by a low inflation outcome for the September quarter.

Comments from New Zealand First leader Winston Peters that the Kiwi was over-valued, and a statement from the Reserve Bank that thoughts of an easing in monetary policy were premature, have both acted to give the currency convulsions.
But for the time being, dealers do not expect the Kiwi to break out of its current range unless fresh factors emerge.
